candidates.name: Kiyomizu-dera autumn night illumination
candidates.reason: The intake's assumed anchor event. The temple's own 2026 event page confirms the autumn night-viewing runs Nov 21-30, 2026 — entirely after this trip's Nov 13-17 window. Cannot be the anchor for these dates; the temple is retained as a daytime sight instead.

candidates.name: Wanaka
candidates.reason: Same quality as the Dotonbori branch; worth a stop only if visiting Kuromon Ichiba anyway, best before 11am.

candidates.name: Kukuru
candidates.reason: Redundant with Wanaka; not independently fetched/verified this pass.

candidates.name: Aizuya
candidates.reason: Not independently verified; redundant with Wanaka/Kukuru in the same category.

candidates.name: Chibo
candidates.reason: Larger tourist-chain feel versus Mizuno's Bib Gourmand pick; not independently fetched this pass.

candidates.name: Fukutaro
candidates.reason: Noted as a local alternative in secondary sources but not independently verified this pass.

candidates.name: Kushikatsu Daruma
candidates.reason: The 1929 flagship — walk-in only, further out in Naniwa-ku. Worth it as its own pilgrimage, not a swap for the convenient Dotonbori branch.

candidates.name: Sushi Tsune
candidates.reason: Called the 'birthplace of battera' in secondary coverage but branch/hours not verified this pass.

candidates.name: Endo Sushi
candidates.reason: Good early-morning market breakfast option, but hours/pricing rest on a single aggregator snippet, not a fetched official source.

candidates.name: Kinryu Ramen
candidates.reason: 24/7 and convenient for a late arrival, but reviews are split ('fine, not exceptional') and ramen isn't a specifically Osaka dish — kept only as a low-effort arrival-night option, not a shipped meal.

candidates.name: Ichiran
candidates.reason: Fukuoka-style chain, not an Osaka specialty; lower priority for a food-first Osaka itinerary.

candidates.name: Chukasoba Kazura
candidates.reason: Repeatedly cited by locals-focused roundups as worth a queue, but not independently verified via an official site or Tabelog this pass.

candidates.name: Kani Doraku
candidates.reason: Iconic mechanical-crab landmark, but ¥5,000-10,000/person with reviews split on ingredient quality (some report frozen crab, display-only tanks). Kept as a photo stop, not a booked meal.

candidates.name: Gion Nishikawa
candidates.reason: Full kaiseki, ¥12,650 (lunch) to ¥33,000 (dinner) per person — well above this trip's mid-range budget. Kept as the reference point for what full foreign-booking friction looks like at the top tier.

candidates.name: Kyomachiya Obanzai Kohaku
candidates.reason: Lower-cost obanzai backup to Houshoan, but only seen via aggregator search snippets — not independently fetched this pass.

candidates.name: Pontocho Izumoya
candidates.reason: A lower-cost Pontocho alternative to Houshoan on paper (≈¥6,600-11,000 kaiseki dinner), but not independently fetched this pass.

candidates.name: Kyoto Kamo Soba Den
candidates.reason: A casual duck-soba spot better suited to lunch than the dinner slot; redundant with existing lunch coverage.

candidates.name: Tsujiri
candidates.reason: Redundant with Nakamura Tokichi in the same area; kept as a backup if the wait there is too long.

candidates.name: Izasa
candidates.reason: Second-floor views over Todai-ji/Nara Park make it a strong pick, but sourcing rests on a single aggregator snippet, not fetched — Tanaka has the stronger official-tourism-site citation, so it ships instead.

candidates.name: Kakinohazushi Hiraso
candidates.reason: Smaller takeaway-only branch, redundant with Tanaka/Izasa's better eat-in options.

candidates.name: Azekuraya
candidates.reason: Chagayu (tea porridge) specialist right on the Todai-ji grounds — a strong lead, but its official site was never independently fetched this pass (aggregator snippet only), so it did not clear the bar to ship for a day-trip lunch with a specific opening window (≈11:00-15:00) to plan around.

candidates.name: Tou No Cha-Ya
candidates.reason: Redundant with Azekuraya; its location relative to Todai-ji was not verified this pass.

candidates.name: Kinkaku-ji
candidates.reason: Exterior-viewing only (no interior access), a single-angle photo-op, and geographically isolated from the Higashiyama/Arashiyama corridor already covered — poor time-efficiency for a balanced-pace 5-day trip.

candidates.name: Arashiyama Monkey Park
candidates.reason: Steep 20-30 min climb for a non-guaranteed close monkey encounter; Nature is the lowest of the three ranked priorities, so it doesn't justify the time slot against Tenryu-ji/the bamboo grove.

candidates.name: Kyoto Tower
candidates.reason: Generic paid observation deck, mediocre view for the cost, no cultural substance beyond the view itself.

candidates.name: Nara National Museum
candidates.reason: Considered as a rain-day indoor alternate for the Nara day trip; its official page (narahaku.go.jp) returned HTTP 403 on two separate fetch attempts, and hours/fee are only corroborated via search-preview — did not clear the bar to ship as a sourced plan_b.

candidates.name: Kansai Railway Pass Lite
candidates.reason: Formerly the Kansai Thru Pass. Its 2026 sales/validity window is Apr 1-Oct 2 only — not usable at all for a Nov 13-17 trip. Also excludes JR lines entirely regardless of season.

candidates.name: JR West Kansai Area Pass
candidates.reason: Valid in November, but doesn't cover the Kintetsu Nara Line used for the day trip, and pay-as-you-go ICOCA plus single Haruka tickets comes out roughly even or cheaper for this itinerary's actual mix of ~4 medium-length rides over 5 days.

candidates.name: ICOCA & HARUKA combo ticket
candidates.reason: Discontinued Sept 30, 2023, replaced by the standalone Haruka one-way ticket products used in this guide.

candidates.name: Welcome Suica
candidates.reason: Sold at Haneda/Narita/central Tokyo JR East locations only, not at KIX — irrelevant to a Kansai-only itinerary; ICOCA is the JR West equivalent product actually available here.

disagreements.topic: Whether the intake's assumed anchor event (Kiyomizu-dera autumn night illumination) actually falls within the trip's Nov 13-17, 2026 dates
disagreements.investigation: Checked the temple's own official event page (kiyomizudera.or.jp/event/yakan.php) directly, corroborated by the neighborhood shopping association's page (monzenkai.com/yakan) — both independently state Nov 21-30, 2026 for the 2026 autumn night viewing, entirely after the trip's end date.
disagreements.resolution: The anchor event cannot be the trip's anchor as assumed. Kiyomizu-dera is retained as a daytime-only sight; a question card was added to the ledger for the traveler, and the days/sights content was written accordingly rather than assuming the illumination happens.

disagreements.topic: Whether physical ICOCA card sales were suspended during the 2023-24 IC-card chip shortage (an assumption stated in the research brief)
disagreements.investigation: Checked JR West's own ICOCA page (jr-odekake.net/icoca/) directly — no suspension notice found. Secondary Japanese-language coverage indicates the chip-shortage suspension affected Suica/PASMO named-card sales specifically (JR East), not ICOCA (JR West).
disagreements.resolution: The premise was likely a conflation of ICOCA with Suica/PASMO. The guide still recommends buying an ICOCA on arrival but carries an explicit ⚠ to confirm at the KIX counter, since no single source fully closed the question this pass.

disagreements.topic: Kiyomizu-dera's regular admission fee (¥500/¥200) could not be confirmed on the temple's own fetched fee page — only on its neighborhood association's page and a third-party aggregator
disagreements.investigation: Fetched kiyomizudera.or.jp/en/visit/, /en/location/, and /en/faq/ directly — none displayed the fee figure in the retrieved content (each referenced a separate page/table not resolved in this pass's fetches). monzenkai.com (the temple's neighborhood shopping association) and an aggregator (kyototravel.info) both independently state ¥500/¥200.
disagreements.resolution: Shipped as an operator-corroborated figure (tier: corroborated) rather than a directly-confirmed official one, flagged in the sight's own note for reconfirmation.

transport.notApplicableReason: Every backbone route researched (KIX transfer, Osaka-Kyoto, both Nara day-trip legs) is a frequent (15-30 min headway) urban/suburban rail service with no single point of failure and generous evening service — none rated above R1-R2, so no route reaches the R3+ transport-depth threshold.

saturation.note: Late-round Osaka food searches (Chukasoba Kazura, Fukutaro, additional battera/sushi spots) mostly surfaced options that were either redundant with already-shortlisted picks or too weakly sourced to ship, not new strong contenders. Kyoto/Nara sights searches converged on the same handful of marquee stops with consistent crowd-timing advice across independent blogs. Remaining unresolved items (the JR Nara Line's exact official fare page, Nara National Museum's blocked official page, a few restaurant hours) are backbone-confirmation gaps, not open questions that would change which candidates are recommended — they're flagged for Pass B/reconcile rather than blocking this pass.
